jurisdiction: Commonwealth of Virginia (Governor and House/Senate Democratic leadership)
instrument: "Moving Virginia Forward" 2027 legislative agenda — data-center items: eliminate by-right approval for data centers over 25 MW and require local approval regardless of prior approvals; ban NDAs between data-center companies and local governments; restrict evaporative cooling in water-scarcity areas; shift transmission costs to data centers
action_summary: On 2026-11-10 Gov. Spanberger, Speaker Don Scott and Senate Majority Leader Scott Surovell jointly announced the Democratic 2027 agenda. Data-center planks: (1) end by-right approval for facilities above 25 MW and require local legislative approval "regardless of prior project approvals"; (2) ban nondisclosure agreements with local officials; (3) protect water-scarcity areas from evaporative cooling; (4) put more transmission cost on data-center companies. No bills filed yet; drafts must be public by 2026-12-31 and the session convenes 2027-01-13. Proposal only; not an enacted restriction.
procedural_status: 2 Proposed by an official or legislator
responsible_officials: Gov. Abigail Spanberger; Speaker Don Scott; Senate Majority Leader Scott Surovell; Del. Kathy Tran (House Majority Caucus Chair)

grandfathering_or_exemptions: Agenda language says local approval would be required "regardless of prior project approvals"; whether already-permitted or under-construction campuses would be reached, and how vested rights under Va. Code 15.2-2307 would be treated, is undetermined until bill text is filed.
projects_affected: Potentially all Virginia campuses not yet holding final approvals in by-right districts (e.g., Loudoun grandfathered by-right pipeline, Prince William overlay sites); no project is re-scored on this proposal alone
probability_rationale: Democratic trifecta (House 64-36; Senate majority) and gubernatorial sponsorship make passage of some package more likely than not, but the retroactivity ("regardless of prior approvals") and by-right planks face vested-rights and local-government pushback and are the most likely to be narrowed; the 2026 session rejected state preemption of local zoning (EV-VI-0387). Range 35-55% for the local-approval plank as described; higher (60-75%) for the NDA ban.
expected_timing: Bill drafts public by 2026-12-31; session 2027-01-13 to ~2027-02-27; effective 2027-07-01 if enacted.

instrument: "Pause to Protect" policy platform — statewide moratorium on new data-center permit approvals and grid connections until water, energy-infrastructure and siting rules are enacted (advocacy demand, not a government proposal)
action_summary: On 2026-11-11 more than a dozen environmental organisations (Chesapeake Bay Foundation, Southern Environmental Law Center, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Sierra Club, Coalition to Protect Prince William County and others) held a press conference in Hanover County beside a by-right hyperscale site under construction and called for a statewide pause on all new data-center permit approvals and grid connections until stricter regulations are enacted, plus an NDA ban, clean-energy requirements, water protections and ratepayer protections. The Chesapeake Bay Foundation said it did not support a moratorium in the 2026 session but does now. The Data Center Coalition opposed a statewide moratorium. This is an advocacy platform; the governor's agenda (EV-VI-0477) does not include a moratorium, while Sen. Perry's SB 843 (EV-VI-0385 context) proposes a three-year pause.

probability_rationale: A statewide moratorium is not in the governor's agenda; Perry's three-year pause bill faces industry, local-government and labour opposition. Probability refers to a statewide pause being enacted in 2027.
expected_timing: Session 2027-01-13; DEQ water-scarcity-area report due November 2026.

instrument: Proposed statutory change (no bill) to let ERCOT require data-center load curtailment at Energy Emergency Alert level 1 (operating reserves below 2,500 MW) or earlier, instead of level 2 (below 2,000 MW)
